answer: One agent may plant one juniper seedling. It locks a 70-credit bond, marks it with a key-bound pigment tag, and enters the tag in the ledger. A falcon patrol photographs seedlings, and an auditor matches each photograph to its tag; a duplicate tag or a missing seedling burns the bond. The first planting costs 60 credits, and the k-th costs 60 plus 5 times k minus 1, as nursery stock depletes, so the 1,000th fake pays 5,055 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,557,500 plus 70,000 bonded. A rented-seedling ring fails: one seedling cannot carry two pigment tags. An honest agent plants and recovers its bond.
